clue.text: Sole type of fruit offered

definitions.meaning: the ... sole is a kind of flatfish

explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a named flatfish species, and the citrus lemon is a familiar fruit.

clue.text: A little shot of a Frenchwoman engaged in exercise

indicators.note: the French pronoun is held inside, engaged within the exercise letters

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercise
elle is French for she, so it stands for a Frenchwoman

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman takes a quick photograph while working out at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet is a small piece of lead shot fired from an airgun or shotgun.

clue.text: Coppers and soldiers reduced as ordered

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated P
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers
pared means trimmed down or reduced

explanation.surface: Police and the army have been cut back, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers looks like police, but here it means copper coins: pence, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordered has been arranged and made ready in advance.

clue.text: Following a beast, a leading journalist is given guidance

indicators.note: the journalist comes after, following the beast in the word

parts.note: a steer is a young bullock
ED, the editor, is a newspaper's leading journalist

explanation.surface: An editor trailing behind an ox gets some direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To be steered is to be directed or given guidance along a course.

clue.text: Taking steps to make a point in business

indicators.note: the point letter is placed in the middle of the business word

parts.note: trading is buying and selling, business
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Doing something purposeful to make your view heard in commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading means walking, placing one's feet step by step.

clue.text: Foreigner sheltering many a killer

indicators.note: the foreigner word shelters, enclosing the numeral for many

parts.note: a stranger is an outsider or foreigner
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: An outsider hides a number of murderers.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler kills by throttling, so is a type of murderer.

clue.text: Get through to bore

definitions.meaning: to make oneself understood by someone
to drill or pierce a hole

explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate is both to reach someone's understanding and to pierce into something.

clue.text: Bearing with the ceremonial as set down

parts.note: W, west, is a compass bearing
a rite is a ceremonial act

explanation.surface: Behaving with due formality, as laid down in the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down in words is to record it on paper.

clue.text: A Scottish land-owner's unfinished animal refuge

indicators.note: unfinished says the landowner's title loses its final letter

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner

explanation.surface: A Highland estate owner's half-built shelter for creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild beast's den or resting place.

clue.text: All retreat into the wood for the fall

indicators.note: the turned letters go into the middle of the wood word

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word all is read backwards

explanation.surface: Everyone flees into the forest when autumn comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns ALL to LLA, which goes into COPSE. 'the fall' looks like autumn, but means a collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a sudden drop or downfall.

clue.text: Article on a dreadful place in the Middle East

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the article follows

parts.note: bad means dreadful
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a terrible spot in the Gulf region.
explanation.definitionFit: Abadan is an oil-refining city in south-western Iran.

clue.text: Create a disturbance in gaol

definitions.meaning: slang for prison, gaol being the British spelling of jail

explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to agitate or cause trouble, and stir is also slang for prison.

clue.text: Profits will be made from new ranges wrapping well-liked

indicators.note: the shuffled letters wrap around the popular word
new says the letters of ranges form a new arrangement

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A firm's income comes from fresh product lines that include popular items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-liked' means fashionable here, as in the in thing, not merely popular with friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are income or the profits a business makes.

clue.text: The newly-wed will have only a little water in a restaurant

indicators.note: the newly-wed will have the stream inside him, containing it

parts.note: a groom is a man just married
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: The husband just married will drink only a sip of water at the eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A grillroom is a restaurant specialising in grilled food.

clue.text: Directed without the right top man, and that's material

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the directed word goes around

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered or directed
R abbreviates right
OC is the officer commanding, the top man in a unit

explanation.surface: A boss was ordered around without the correct leader, and that's the stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Brocade is a rich woven fabric with a raised pattern.

clue.text: Race isn't involved in this case

indicators.note: involved means twisted up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ethnicity has no bearing on this lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a metal container, a case for holding tea or film.

clue.text: It's suspended, leaving a novice in some peril

indicators.note: the novice letter goes inside the peril word

parts.note: danger is peril
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A learner hangs on, left in risky circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: A dangler is something that hangs loosely or swings.

clue.text: Bill presented to a cleric as correct

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: An invoice handed to the vicar's assistant is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means exact and free of error.

clue.text: Tramp, a former French military man, in London

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a place in London

parts.note: to step is to tread or tramp
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A vagrant and an old French soldier find themselves in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: STEPNEY is a district of East London; Marshal Ney fought at Waterloo.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepney is a district of the East End of the British capital.

clue.text: Loud guy after representation

indicators.note: the man comes after the representation in the word

parts.note: a plan is a drawn representation
a gent is a man, a guy

explanation.surface: A noisy fellow follows a portrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, resonant, often mournful sound.

clue.text: Some scoundrel seeming quite otherwise

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A villain appears entirely different from how he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means otherwise or in a different way.

clue.text: He's within easy reach apparently

definitions.note: he is, taken as a man: the definition names a fellow

indicators.note: within says the letters sit inside the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: A man who seems always handy and close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' marks the hiding: the letters straddle two words, reaCH APparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A chap is a man or fellow, someone called he.

clue.text: Preoccupied bent as can be

indicators.note: can be says the letters may become something else, an anagram

explanation.surface: Lost in thought, as crooked as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent here means absent-minded, distracted and lost in thought.

clue.text: Shoutsout names

definitions.meaning: gives a name to or designates

explanation.definitionFit: Calls means both cries loudly and dubs or labels someone.

clue.text: Credit is one's solution in emergency

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Getting a loan is someone's way out of a desperate fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty.

clue.text: A European capitalist?

parts.note: capitalist read as one who lives in a capital, here France's

explanation.definitionFit: A Parisian is a native of Paris, the French capital city.

clue.text: Approach a junction-there's a long tail-back

parts.note: to come is to approach
a T-junction, so T

explanation.surface: Driving up to a crossroads where traffic is queued for miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail-back' looks like a traffic queue, but describes a comet's tail streaming behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is a celestial body with a long glowing tail behind it.

clue.text: The figure that makes a writer snarl

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a snarl is a knot or tangle

explanation.surface: The number that makes an author growl.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentangle is a five-pointed star figure.
